correctness.rationale: For output height θ≥0, the spatial minimizers are coordinate clips, and the remaining scalar objective is strictly convex. On a strict clipped support S the active height-spatial derivative block is the rank-one orthogonal projector in direction (1,(σ_i a_i)_{i∈S}); the unclipped block is identity. The specified input at θ=1 realizes every S in an open chart, so segment integration and small row-sign perturbations give equality in the global formula. At an optimal subset for R, every unforced included a is ≤1/R and every excluded a is ≥1/R, by deletion and insertion, respectively. Ties can be ordered as a prefix. This proves the candidate count both with no forced coordinate and with one forced. Singletons give strict expansion at any non-unit reciprocal weight. For k active coordinates, a rank-one orthogonal projector in dimension k+1 has maximum row sum bounded by (1+√(k+1))/2: writing q for its diagonal entry, Cauchy–Schwarz bounds the row by q+√(kq(1−q)). Equality at the ambient ceiling forces full support and a distinguished coordinate larger in magnitude than every other coordinate by √(n+1)+1, the other magnitudes being equal. Normalizing the height coordinate gives exactly the n+1 listed positive designs; strict chart realization attains the bound. For the positive dual at unit weights, the active block is the complementary hyperplane projector with row sum 2k/(k+1); full support is feasible and gives the claimed constant. The negative polar has the same modulus by reflection. The frozen script was inspected, not executed.

evidence: Liu et al. p. 738 explicitly announce exact directional derivatives, B-subdifferentials and Clarke generalized Jacobians for the same two weighted epigraphs. Ding–Sun–Toh treat unweighted or uniformly scaled cases. The indexed Lorentz theorem contains the same ceiling (1+√d)/2 for its axial branch in ambient dimension d+1, but with a Euclidean spatial norm.
For any orthogonal projector in N coordinates, the row diagonal q fixes the off-diagonal squared row mass at q(1−q), giving the general ceiling (1+√N)/2 independently of epigraph structure.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Prior derivative theory is real coverage, as is the generic bound as a mathematical implication of idempotence. Neither the general ceiling alone nor the Lorentz example identifies all heterogeneous weights realizing it in the specified maximum-norm epigraph.

evidence: The indexed ℓ1 proof gives J=I−vvᵀ/(1+Σ_{i∈S}a_i²) on the active coordinates and height, with zero inactive rows and all strict supports realized. Moreau gives the frozen derivative as the complement of that matrix at the reflected input. Its row sums are R(S), a_iR(S) and 1. The same threshold exchange in the indexed proof applies to these ratios; singleton rigidity then follows directly.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The reduction credits exact chart and subset-modulus implications and the shared prefix method. The unrestricted optimum and complete designs require a further equality analysis across all supports and reciprocal weights: no proper support can saturate the ambient bound, and the equality row forces one distinguished magnitude. This produces the specific two types of weight vectors, not a change of variables in the indexed product-constrained ℓ1 optimum.

evidence: With a_i=1/w_i, the positive dual of the frozen cone is the indexed weighted ℓ1 epigraph K_a. That record proves 2n/(n+1) at equal unit weights, and its weight-design theorem in the Finding fixes a product constraint in the plane and concerns K_a, not its dual projector.
Chierchia et al. give the weighted coordinate clipping and scalar minimizer for the exact frozen cone.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Moreau converts the complete chart matrices, but the norm of I−J is not determined by the norm of J. In particular their product-constrained planar ℓ1 design theorem is not an equivalent formulation of the unrestricted all-dimensional maximum-epigraph design equality cases.

evidence: The first supplies the exact unit-weight polar constant; the second supplies the same dimension-dependent number on a different cone. Neither states the n+1 maximum-epigraph designs.
exact_database_or_table.reasoning: The exact design is an analytic continuum optimization, not a finite catalogue or census. Matching constant values without matching the cone and attainable weight vectors do not establish the design theorem.

originality.rationale: Pass for the exact unconstrained design maximum for the weighted maximum-norm epigraph together with the exhaustive classification of its attaining weight vectors. Credit the earlier projection and derivative theory; the exact subset modulus is also a direct Moreau-complement consequence of the matching indexed weighted ℓ1 chart matrices, and the unweighted dual comparison is already covered. The generic matrix ceiling, taken alone, is not a distinct result. None of the inspected sources optimizes across reciprocal-weight designs for the maximum-norm epigraph or identifies which weights realize the ceiling; that requires the full-support and equality optimization, not just a numeric ceiling or duality of the cones. The unresolved complete-text comparison with Liu et al. limits this judgment. No priority conclusion is made from catalogue dates.
residual_risks: The later sections of Liu et al. (2015) were not recovered for inspection; exact global conclusions in them remain an open bibliographic risk.
The bounded comparison does not rule out another known source explicitly optimizing all reciprocal weights or supplying an immediate equivalent equality classification.

value.rationale: The coordinatewise perturbation question is natural because Euclidean nonexpansivity does not control the largest coordinate error sharply. Beyond the generic ceiling, the design theorem says whether it is realized by this specific family and gives every calibrating weight vector that realizes it, distinguishing height and spatial failure modes. These exact equality cases are useful for choosing or ruling out worst-case anisotropic calibrations. The covered polar example is not counted separately.
